title: Standard-library sandboxing: settlement key unreachable from any primitive (A24)
question: Does the capability model demonstrate the pre-repair key path, its absence under uniform sandboxing, and enforcement of identical terms?

registered_notes.defect: A24: the standard library runs directly in the signing process while only third-party code is sandboxed; the settlement key lives in a host process
registered_notes.pinning: trusted-by-hash guarantees you run the intended code, including its intended bugs, on attacker-chosen input
registered_notes.repair: R-A24: sandbox the standard library on the same terms as third-party primitives

interpretation_registered_before_running.c1_fails: the pre-repair model shows no key path - the registered defect would not be demonstrated; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c2_fails: a path to the key remains after sandboxing - the repair does not close A24; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.c3_fails: elevated or missing terms pass the guard - the uniform-terms policy is not enforced; VOID
interpretation_registered_before_running.all_hold: M317 PASS: the sandbox policy closes A24 at the registered cells
